gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro, a single added 16-inch 2560×1600 120 Hz screen, is $247.99 on mobilepixels.us on 2026-11-21, under the $250 line. Legit Product Reviews lists it at $263.49, dated 2026-10-31, and DeskGearHQ leaves it out.
standout_why: I compared the two cited rival pages. Legit Product Reviews (updated 2026-11-09, prices dated 2026-10-31) lists the Duex Float 2 Pro at $263.49, which is over $250. It says the screen has been at that price since at least August 2026 and calls that its real price. DeskGearHQ's guide (verified July 2026) leaves the Float 2 Pro out and lists the Duex Max DS at $199.99. Neither page has a price read today, during the Black Friday sale. Neither page shows that a 16-inch 2.5K 120 Hz single screen is inside a $250 budget. ChatGPT's two answers named only 13.3–15.6-inch 1080p screens and one 14-inch 2K screen.
decides: This confirms the Duex Max DS as the default pick. It is a 14.1-inch 1080p screen that slides out from behind the lid on magnets, and it is $215.99 through our link today. It drives over one USB-C DisplayPort Alt Mode cable with no driver, or over USB-C plus mini HDMI. The finding adds a second row of ours that fits the question: the Duex Float 2 Pro at $247.99. It wins the segment for owners of 15–16-inch laptops (Mobile Pixels' fit range) who want one bigger, sharper screen above the laptop instead of beside it. That row is $2.01 under the budget because of a timed Mobile Pixels sale. Mobile Pixels' prices move with these sales (the Trio 3 Pro went from $367.99 on 2026-11-18 to $407.99 on 2026-11-21), so the page should say the Float 2 Pro's place depends on today's price. No sale end date was found. The cheaper options (Duex Plus DS and Mobile Pixels Fold / Glance) lose either on size (13.3-inch) or because they stand next to the laptop instead of attaching to it.
